decision: Preserve the salvage branch and work on daoa/recovery-architecture.
trigger: Architecture recovery must not overwrite prior work.
outcome: Recovery changes are isolated; commit 68d353b remains the salvage point.

decision: Reject recorded-session conditions in production code.
trigger: An exact Wizard-level raven condition and fixed Oracle display draws were active.
alternatives: Keep narrow exceptions until matching owners are ported.
outcome: Deleted the branches and added tools/architecture-audit.mjs.

decision: Use CORE for Lua random calls and do not add a Lua RNG.
trigger: The pinned nhlib.lua replaces math.random with nh.rn2 and nh.random.
alternatives: Use Lua's built-in RNG or add a third context.
outcome: The Lua runtime contract has exactly CORE and DISP.

decision: Refactor the current game runner into the engine owner instead of wrapping it.
trigger: A wrapper would leave two session owners and duplicate lifecycle state.
alternatives: Add an Engine facade around NethackGame.
outcome: One Engine will own state, input, display, capture, RNG, storage, and the running task.

decision: Treat missing input as an InputGate state.
trigger: The old runner threw from GameDisplay and caught a message string in a bounded loop.
alternatives: Keep the terminal exception or add a second outer driver.
outcome: Engine.runningTask now suspends at one gate and runSegment returns when that gate reports input-needed.

decision: Save only schema-listed game data and link entities by stable IDs.
trigger: Enumerable snapshots mixed runtime handles with persistent state and restored only the active map prototype.
alternatives: Keep an omit list or serialize every object independently.
outcome: Version 2 rejects unclassified fields, preserves shared object and monster identity, and rehydrates cached maps.

decision: Implement the pinned Lua syntax in JavaScript and package source as browser modules.
trigger: Fengari targets Lua 5.3 and the game cannot use WASM, files, or network access at runtime.
alternatives: Adopt Lua 5.3 or continue translating each Lua file by hand.
outcome: The minimal 5.4 state lifecycle now parses and executes nhlib.lua and nhcore.lua; later slices extend the same runtime for level scripts.

decision: Load dungeon definitions by executing dungeon.lua.
trigger: Startup used a copied JavaScript table even though the parser can execute the source data unchanged.
alternatives: Keep the copied table as a fallback.
outcome: The copied table was deleted; dungeon.c placement rules now consume Lua-produced definitions.

decision: Allow MATCH_WALL at the center of a map fragment.
trigger: The JavaScript check rejected every terrain value above MAX_TYPE, but C rejects only MAX_TYPE and INVALID_TYPE.
outcome: Big Room, Hell, and Wizard wall-pattern selections build successfully.

decision: Delete the seeded role-outcome test harness.
trigger: Its tests chose generated worlds by seed and compared flattened outcomes, so correct startup RNG changes invalidated unrelated scheduler claims.
alternatives: Update the expected coordinates, move counts, inventories, and actor snapshots.
outcome: Constructed-state mechanic tests remain; the test tree is 935 lines smaller.
